articles.before: CVE-2025-23120 KB ID: 4724 Product: Veeam Backup & Replication | 12 | 12.1 | 12.2 | 12.3 Published: 2025-03-19 Last Modified: 2026-10-29 Veeam Software Security Commitment Veeam® is committed to ensuring its products protect customers from potential risks. As part of that commitment, we operate a Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) for all Veeam products and perform extensive internal code audits. When a vulnerability is identified, our team promptly develops a patch to address and mitigate the risk. In line with our dedication to transparency, we publicly disclose the vulnerability and provide detailed mitigation information. This approach ensures that all potentially affected customers can quickly implement the necessary measures to safeguard their systems. It’s important to note that once a vulnerability and its associated patch are disclosed, attackers will likely attempt to reverse-engineer the patch to exploit unpatched deployments of Veeam software. This reality underscores the critical importance of ensuring that all customers use the latest versions of our software and install all updates and patches without delay. Issue Details CVE-2025-23120 A vulnerability allowing remote code execution (RCE) on the Backup Server by an authenticated domain user. Severity: Critical CVSS v3.1 Score: 9.9 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H Source: Reported by Piotr Bazydlo of watchTowr . Note: This vulnerability only impacts domain-joined backup servers. Veeam Backup & Replication Security Best Practice Guide > Workgroup or Domain? Affected Product Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3.0.310 and all earlier version 12 builds . Note: Unsupported product versions are not tested, but are likely affected and should be considered vulnerable. Solution The vulnerability documented in this section was fixed starting in the following build: Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3.1 (build 12.3.1.1139)

Article Updates Veeam is investigating these vulnerabilities and will update this article as new information becomes available. Summary nginx2root is the common name for five memory corruption vulnerabilities in nginx: CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634, and CVE-2026-113425. They affect the HTTP/2 module, the HTTP/3 module, the DNS resolver, and the mail proxy, and can be triggered remotely. Combined with a Linux kernel vulnerability, they can lead to root access. Windows-based installations of Veeam Backup & Replication and Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager do not use nginx and are not affected. Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance include nginx and are listed in the following table. Whether a Veeam component is affected depends on the nginx build it includes and the nginx features its configuration enables. The following table lists the status and the required action for each product. Product Affected Action Veeam Software Appliance 13.1 Yes, a fix is not yet available Restrict access to TCP port 443 to trusted networks Windows-based Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 No. nginx is not used. No action is required Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager 13.1 on Linux No. HTTP/2 is not enabled. No action is required Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager 13.1 on Windows No. nginx is not used. No action is required Workers deployed by Veeam Plug-Ins for hypervisors No. The affected nginx features are not used. No action is required Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 Yes, a fix is not yet available Restrict access to TCP port 443 to trusted networks Veeam Plug-In for AWS , Veeam Plug-In for Google Cloud , and Veeam Plug-In for Microsoft Azure appliances Yes, until the nginx update is installed Install all available security updates through Veeam Updater Veeam Data Cloud for Salesforce , Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure , and Veeam Data Cloud for AWS Yes, remediation by Veeam is in progress No customer action is required Veeam Backup for Salesforce 3.2.1 Yes, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 Install the operating system vendor update or disable HTTP/2 Swipe to show more of the table Solution Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 include an affected nginx build with HTTP/2 enabled. A fixed nginx package is not yet available. The fixed package will be delivered through Veeam Updater , and this article will be updated when it is available. HTTP/2 cannot be disabled on these appliances because Veeam components depend on it. Until the fixed package is installed, restrict access to TCP port 443 on the appliances to trusted networks. Public Cloud Appliances The Veeam Plug-In for AWS , Veeam Plug-In for Google Cloud , and Veeam Plug-In for Microsoft Azure appliances run Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and use the nginx package provided by Ubuntu. The patched nginx package ( 1.18.0-6ubuntu14.23 ) is installed with the security updates offered through Veeam Updater . Worker instances do not include nginx and are not affected. To remediate the vulnerabilities, install all available security updates through Veeam Updater. Veeam Data Cloud Veeam manages the infrastructure of Veeam Data Cloud for Salesforce , Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure , and Veeam Data Cloud for AWS , and is remediating the affected services. No customer action is required. Veeam Backup for Salesforce Veeam Backup for Salesforce 3.2.1 uses the nginx package provided by the operating system of the server where it is installed, and generates the nginx configuration. That configuration enables HTTP/2 on a listener that proxies requests to a backend, so CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 apply. The remaining vulnerabilities do not apply to this configuration. Veeam does not manage the operating system or the nginx package on customer-deployed Veeam Backup for Salesforce servers. Customers managing these servers are advised to review the advisory from the operating system vendor and install the nginx update when it is available. Until the nginx update is installed, HTTP/2 can be disabled to remediate the vulnerabilities: On the Veeam Backup for Salesforce server, open the following file: /etc/nginx/sites-available/vbsf-frontend.conf Remove the http2 parameter from the listen directive for port 443. Change: listen 443 ssl http2; to: listen 443 ssl; Save the file, then check the nginx configuration and restart the nginx service: sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl restart nginx.service Copy More Information CVE-2026-123007 | NVD CVE-2026-123633 | NVD CVE-2026-121810 | NVD CVE-2026-123634 | NVD CVE-2026-113425 | NVD

Article Updates Veeam is investigating these vulnerabilities and will update this article as new information becomes available. Summary nginx2root is the common name for five memory corruption vulnerabilities in nginx: CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634, and CVE-2026-113425. They affect the HTTP/2 module, the HTTP/3 module, the DNS resolver, and the mail proxy, and can be triggered remotely. Combined with a Linux kernel vulnerability, they can lead to root access. Windows-based installations of Veeam Backup & Replication and Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager do not use nginx and are not affected. Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance include nginx and are listed in the following table. Whether a Veeam component is affected depends on the nginx build it includes and the nginx features its configuration enables. The following table lists the status and the required action for each product. Product Affected Notes Veeam Software Appliance 13.1 Yes Affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. Install the latest security updates through Veeam Updater . Windows-based Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 No nginx is not used. Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager 13.1 on Linux No HTTP/2 is not enabled. Veeam Backup Enterprise Manager 13.1 on Windows No nginx is not used. Workers deployed by Veeam Plug-Ins for hypervisors No The affected nginx features are not used. Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 Yes Affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. Install the latest security updates through Veeam Updater . Veeam Plug-In for AWS , Veeam Plug-In for Google Cloud , and Veeam Plug-In for Microsoft Azure appliances Yes Install all available security updates through Veeam Updater . Veeam Data Cloud for Salesforce , Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure , and Veeam Data Cloud for AWS Yes Veeam manages these services. No customer action required . Veeam Backup for Salesforce 3.2.1 Yes Affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. Install the operating system vendor update or disable HTTP/2 . Swipe to show more of the table Solution Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 include an nginx build with HTTP/2 enabled on a listener that proxies requests to a backend, so CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 apply. The remaining vulnerabilities do not apply to the appliance configuration. Since November 25, 2026, an update that contains the fix has been available in the Veeam repository for Veeam Software Appliance and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 ( nginx-1.20.1-22.8.el9_6_ciq.3 ). To remediate the vulnerabilities, install the latest security updates through Veeam Updater . Veeam Updater checks the repository every 12 hours. With the default update configuration, mandatory updates are installed automatically on the nearest Sunday at 14:00, based on the time zone of the backup server. If the update does not appear on the Updates tab, it may already be installed. To confirm, check the History tab in the Veeam Host Management console. For details, see Veeam Backup & Replication User Guide: Viewing Update History . Appliances that use a local mirror of the Veeam repository receive the update after the mirror is synchronized. To install the update without waiting for automatic installation, perform the following steps: Log in to the Veeam Host Management console on the backup server. In the management pane, click Updates > Check for updates . On the Updates tab, select the available updates, then click Install Updates Now and confirm the operation. If a backup infrastructure component uses a custom update configuration, repeat these steps in the Veeam Host Management console of that component. Until the update is installed, restrict access to TCP port 443 on the appliances to trusted networks. HTTP/2 cannot be disabled on these appliances because Veeam components depend on it. For more information, see Veeam Backup & Replication User Guide: Configuring Updates and Installing Updates . Public Cloud Appliances The Veeam Plug-In for AWS , Veeam Plug-In for Google Cloud , and Veeam Plug-In for Microsoft Azure appliances run Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and use the nginx package provided by Ubuntu. The patched nginx package ( 1.18.0-6ubuntu14.23 ) is installed with the security updates offered through Veeam Updater . Worker instances do not include nginx and are not affected. To remediate the vulnerabilities, install all available security updates through Veeam Updater. Veeam Data Cloud Veeam manages the infrastructure of Veeam Data Cloud for Salesforce , Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft Azure , and Veeam Data Cloud for AWS , and is responsible for applying security updates to these services. No customer action is required. Veeam Backup for Salesforce Veeam Backup for Salesforce 3.2.1 uses the nginx package provided by the operating system of the server where it is installed, and generates the nginx configuration. That configuration enables HTTP/2 on a listener that proxies requests to a backend, so CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 apply. The remaining vulnerabilities do not apply to this configuration. Veeam does not manage the operating system or the nginx package on customer-deployed Veeam Backup for Salesforce servers. Customers managing these servers are advised to review the advisory from the operating system vendor and install the nginx update when it is available. Until the nginx update is installed, HTTP/2 can be disabled to remediate the vulnerabilities: On the Veeam Backup for Salesforce server, open the following file: /etc/nginx/sites-available/vbsf-frontend.conf Remove the http2 parameter from the listen directive for port 443.
